palette.notes: Palette not the topic of this post.

silhouette: Shape comes from clusters: simple angular clusters give a clean, sharp look; varied organic clusters look natural. Every pixel should be placed on purpose, so the outline reads at 1x.
texture: Hard pixel edges only: no automatic anti-aliasing on brushes or scaling; manual anti-aliasing is deferred to a later post. Detail too fine to notice undermines the pixel look.
camera: Work small (author's pieces around 128x128 to 256x256) and present with whole-number scaling only (2x to 4x; about 4x is the most before it looks too chunky). Figures are the article's.

acting.acts: Staging lesson: intention per pixel; a small canvas forces each element to earn its place.

techniques: intentional pixel placement: every pixel is a decision
cluster shape sets the style: angular = clean, organic = natural
no automatic anti-aliasing anywhere, including on scaling
integer scaling only (200/300/400%) so pixels stay square
start on a small canvas and grow it only when needed
feel: small canvas + deliberate clusters + integer scale = crisp art that reads as pixel art, not a blurry painting
for_fred: Render Fred and Pixie at their native sprite size and scale to the 1080x1920 reel by a whole number with nearest-neighbour, never a fractional or smoothed scale; mixing sprite scales in one shot (e.g. a 3x Fred next to a 4x Pixie) breaks the look, so pick one scale per reel and use whole-sprite size changes only for depth.
